Summary

Backport [#1700](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/csharp-sdk/pull/1700) (7369a265a89d748b86f028fb132f58ba4d22b961) to `release/1.x`, with an explicitly approved 1.x security-default adaptation for metadata-free legacy servers. Also backport only the RFC 8414 authorization-server metadata-issuer checks from [#1605](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/csharp-sdk/pull/1605) (4aade885583e90eed8192721cc35f7b49411464c), preserving its intentional legacy exemption.

The first commit preserves #1700's production change and four regression tests, with cherry-pick attribution. Two test-file conflicts were resolved without importing unrelated scope-selection/offline-access changes. The second commit adds the opt-in compatibility switch described below. The third adds the source-equivalent metadata-issuer checks, related tests/documentation, and the approved test-only conformance package update needed for compliant issuer fixtures. A follow-up changes only the build/test workflow's Node pin from 20 to 22 for the conformance bundle's runtime prerequisite. The latest test-only simplification removes class-wide serialization and testhost switch mutations, retaining default-state tests and the existing conformance subprocess for legacy opt-in coverage.

- Require discovered authorization server metadata to advertise `S256` in `code_challenge_methods_supported`; no longer synthesize that field for discovered documents.
- Continue trying alternative well-known endpoints when a document fails PKCE validation, logging the specific failure. A later eligible document can still succeed.
- Never replace a discovered document that fails PKCE validation with synthetic legacy defaults, regardless of the switch.
- When protected resource metadata is available, require the metadata `issuer` to exactly match the selected authorization server identifier using `OriginalString` and `StringComparison.Ordinal`. Missing/mismatched issuers immediately stop discovery before authorization or token exchange; they are not swallowed, retried against another endpoint, or replaced by synthetic defaults.
- Add no response-aware callback APIs, state-validation backport, or RFC 9207 authorization-response issuer-validation behavior. No main-branch change or unrelated ExceptionDispatchInfo refactor is included.

This supersedes the proposed state-validation backport [#1948](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/csharp-sdk/pull/1948) with a focused 1.x approach, rather than importing the callback architecture from #1605/#1726.

## Deliberate 1.x security-default adaptation

Original #1700 retains the MCP 2025-03-26 default-endpoint fallback when protected resource metadata is unavailable and authorization server metadata discovery finds no usable document. That fallback synthesizes `S256`, which does not establish PKCE support. Because the existing 1.x callback API returns only a code and cannot provide response state for SDK validation, this backport makes that fallback **disabled by default**.

`ModelContextProtocol.Authentication.AllowLegacyOAuthMetadataFallback` is a **default-off, process-wide AppContext switch**. When absent or `false`, the client rejects that metadata-free path before requesting an authorization code or exchanging tokens. A host can explicitly restore only the original eligible fallback at startup:

```csharp
AppContext.SetSwitch(
    "ModelContextProtocol.Authentication.AllowLegacyOAuthMetadataFallback",
    true);
```

The switch retains the original `resourceUri is null` guard, `/authorize`, `/token`, and `/register` defaults, and unchanged `S256` challenge/verifier behavior. It cannot bypass discovered metadata that omits `S256`, and the client logs a warning whenever it actually uses this unverified fallback.

Enabling the switch is **not** verification of PKCE support and does not add state validation. Hosts must independently establish that a trusted deployment correctly enforces PKCE, including downgrade defenses. This is not a per-server allowlist: it affects all OAuth clients in the process. Do not enable it in a process that also connects to untrusted authorization servers or toggle it around individual requests.

The API remarks, transport guide, and protected-client sample documentation explain configuration and security requirements. The conformance client opts in only for its trusted `auth/2025-03-26-oauth-endpoint-fallback` fixture; other scenarios retain the secure default.

## Security rationale

[RFC 9700 §2.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700.html#section-2.1) explicitly states that clients which have ensured authorization-server PKCE support "MAY rely on the CSRF protection provided by PKCE". [§4.7.1](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700.html#section-4.7.1) describes PKCE as an alternative to `state` for CSRF protection and requires clients to establish server support before relying on it. This backport strengthens that prerequisite for existing code-only callbacks without requiring a new callback API or SDK response-state validation.

This verifies **advertised support**, not the server's actual verifier or downgrade implementation. Authorization servers must correctly enforce PKCE, including the [§4.8.2 downgrade defenses](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9700.html#section-4.8.2). This is an alternative for the CSRF protection requirement, not a claim that state validation is universally unnecessary or that this approach is security-equivalent to every state-validation design.

### Metadata issuer validation is included; response issuer validation remains deferred

[RFC 8414 §3.3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8414.html#section-3.3) requires the metadata issuer to be identical to the issuer identifier used for discovery. This PR includes #1605's metadata-only checks without importing its response-aware callback API. Comparisons do not normalize URI case, trailing slashes, or percent-encoding, so previously accepted equivalent-looking issuer strings may now be rejected. The source's `McpException` rethrow path is retained: metadata validation failures stop discovery immediately instead of being logged and silently retried.

As in #1605, these issuer checks are exempt when `resourceUri` is null in the MCP 2025-03-26 legacy path: discovery uses the MCP server's origin rather than an authorization server identifier obtained from protected resource metadata, so it need not equal the canonical issuer. PKCE requirements and the default-off fallback switch remain unchanged.

RFC 9207 authorization-response `iss` validation addresses authorization-server mix-up, a separate threat; PKCE is not a substitute for issuer validation. That **response** check still requires response-aware callback plumbing and remains deferred for servicing scope. Including metadata checks is not a claim that response-issuer validation is unnecessary or that 1.x clients are immune to mix-up attacks.

## Test fixture dependency update

The test-only `@modelcontextprotocol/conformance` pin is updated from `0.1.13` to `0.1.15`, the earliest stable published release correcting the tenant issuer fixtures. In `0.1.13`, `auth/metadata-var2` and `auth/metadata-var3` advertise an authorization server identifier ending in `/tenant1` but return a root metadata issuer, which the new SDK checks correctly reject. [modelcontextprotocol/conformance#152](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance/pull/152), commit [50c3cf1](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/conformance/commit/50c3cf1a430274ebdaaddeb95ef2c786a6bca290), fixes the server-side issuer to include `routePrefix` while preserving the tested discovery paths.

This is not an SDK/client validation bypass or a rewritten fixture. The manifest changes one pin; npm updates its lock entry and adds 20 transitive package entries for the new Octokit dependency chain, leaving existing other package versions unchanged. The newer harness also includes scenario specification-version annotations and a shared auth fixture fix that creates a fresh stateless MCP server per request. The existing selected scenarios and full suite pass without unrelated SDK behavior fixes, further upgrades, skipped scenarios, or weakened assertions.

**CI runtime prerequisite:** The `0.1.15` conformance bundle statically imports `fs.globSync`. The original Node 20 CI pin cannot load it and fails with `SyntaxError: The requested module 'fs' does not provide an export named 'globSync'` before the conformance tests start; this is not an issuer-validation regression. Earlier local validation used Node 24.20.0, where that import works, and therefore missed the CI runtime mismatch. The follow-up changes only `node-version: '20'` to `'22'` in `.github/workflows/ci-build-test.yml`, matching main. The pinned setup-node action, other workflows, npm/dependency pins, SDK behavior, and test expectations are unchanged.

## Release note

**Compatibility tightening:** OAuth authentication now requires discovered authorization server metadata to advertise `S256` PKCE support, even if the server implements PKCE without advertising it. When protected resource metadata is available, authorization server metadata must also provide an `issuer` exactly matching the selected authorization server identifier, without normalizing case, trailing slashes, or percent-encoding. Metadata validation failures immediately stop discovery before authorization or token exchange. The original 2025-03-26 metadata-issuer exemption is preserved when protected resource metadata is unavailable; RFC 9207 authorization-response issuer validation is not added.

Metadata-free legacy authentication is also rejected by default. Trusted 2025-03-26 deployments with independently established PKCE support can explicitly restore the historical no-metadata fallback using the process-wide `ModelContextProtocol.Authentication.AllowLegacyOAuthMetadataFallback` AppContext switch; enabling it emits a warning and never bypasses PKCE validation of discovered metadata.

## Validation

- Latest test-only simplification: solution build passed with zero warnings/errors. All OAuth tests and client conformance scenarios (`--filter 'FullyQualifiedName~ModelContextProtocol.AspNetCore.Tests.OAuth|FullyQualifiedName~ModelContextProtocol.ConformanceTests.ClientConformanceTests'`) passed on .NET 8, 9, and 10 with ordinary parallel test settings: **87 passed per framework**, zero failures/skips. No collection attribute, AppContext usage, switch helper, or switch constant remains in `AuthTests`; the unused nonparallel collection definition was removed.
- Default-state coverage retains secure-default no-metadata rejection, missing/plain-only PKCE rejection including the legacy path, alternative-discovery success, the protected-resource-metadata guard, and meaningful no authorization/token/callback activity and no-fallback-warning assertions.
- Issuer coverage retains matching root/path issuers, missing issuers, mismatched issuers, exact-string case/trailing-slash/percent-encoding rejection, no discovery retry, code-only callback rejection before invocation, no authorization/token activity on rejection, and preserved legacy acceptance with a missing or different canonical issuer.
- Opted-in legacy fallback remains covered by the existing `auth/2025-03-26-oauth-endpoint-fallback` conformance subprocess, unchanged. Explicit false/true switch permutations, opted-in rejection combinations, and the dedicated in-process fallback-success/warning assertion were intentionally removed rather than serializing `AuthTests` or adding new subprocess infrastructure. The testhost no longer mutates the process-wide switch; production behavior and switch caching semantics are unchanged.
- Earlier CI runtime follow-up: solution Debug and Release builds passed with zero warnings/errors. All conformance client/server selections (`--filter 'FullyQualifiedName~Conformance'`) ran under a checksum-verified, process-local **Node 22.23.4**, not the shared host's Node 24: **72 passed, 2 existing Windows skips** on each of .NET 8, 9, and 10 in both configurations (432 passed, 12 skips across the six runs). The `fs.globSync` module import and conformance CLI startup also succeeded. The portable runtime was removed afterward; shared machine settings and the host Node version were not changed.
- Earlier complete non-manual solution suite at the issuer-validation commit, using Node 24.20.0: 8,594 passed, 262 skipped, zero failures across .NET 8/9/10 and .NET Framework 4.7.2. These are historical counts before removal of the redundant switch permutations, not a claim of a new full-suite run for the latest test-only simplification.

Local process tests used a test-process-only current-directory PATH entry for Windows executable lookup. npm installed the approved pinned test-dependency update without lifecycle scripts.
